instruction: Export all emails from the Bills folder in Thunderbird to Google Drive in a folder named 'emails', saving each as an .eml file named by its subject.

metadata.explanation: Verifies that exactly 2 .eml files are uploaded to Google Drive 'emails' folder. The original Bills folder contains 2 emails: one from AWS and one from X (Twitter). Verified by examining the thunderbird-profile.tar.gz Bills folder which contains 2 messages.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Evaluator only verifies file COUNT (2 files), not file TYPE - does not check if files are .eml format
CRITICAL: Evaluator does not verify file NAMING - instruction requires files to be named by their subject, but evaluator ignores filenames
CRITICAL: Evaluator does not verify file CONTENT - cannot confirm that uploaded files are actual emails from the Thunderbird Bills folder

Incomplete coverage: Instruction has 5 requirements (export from Bills, upload to Drive, create 'emails' folder, .eml format, name by subject), but evaluator only verifies quantity and folder location
False positive risk: Evaluator would pass if user uploads any 2 files (e.g., 2 JPG images, 2 text files) to the 'emails' folder, even if they are not .eml files from Thunderbird
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add getter logic to retrieve file metadata (names and mimeTypes) from Google Drive, not just count
Add metric logic to verify all files have .eml extension (check filename ends with '.eml')
Optionally verify file names match expected email subjects (if subject data is available from the Thunderbird profile)
Consider verifying file mimeType is 'message/rfc822' or similar email format, not just any file type
